observations.says: the stove was cold, raked out and shut: no fire came from it
an empty lamp-oil can lay by the press: oil was brought up to it
the books were pulled out and heaped to burn
the fire was laid in the heap of books before the ledger press, and burned deepest there
the iron chest was locked and unbroken, with the duty money in it
the bond store below was unburnt, locked, its seal whole
against: the brandy in the bond store

observations.says: the can by the press is painted C.H.
the oil cupboard in the lamp room stood open, opened with its own key, and the place of the can was empty
neither the door nor its frame is marked
the windows are barred, and the bars are whole
the watch tried the door at twelve and found it fast
against: the door had been left unlocked

observations.says: fast at twelve, and the bolt drawn back after the fire: someone unlocked it in between, and that needed a key
the book is signed at every hour but one o'clock

the pier-head lamp is a quarter of an hour from the watch-box and the Custom House
the harbour log has the bell at 1.45 by the office clock
the office clock is right
Mrs. Rowe took the time from the church clock, and it is half an hour slow
Mrs. Rowe was honest, and wrong
the landlord says he was not in the house when the bell rang
the potboy says his chair was empty
Mr. Prout told me a thing that was not so
Dr. Hume sat with him at Cliff House from half past twelve until a quarter past two
he could not put his foot to the ground
the Marigold sailed at 9.45 on Tuesday night
with high water at 9.30, nothing could cross the bar from 11.30 until 7.55 in the morning
the log is in his hand at midnight and at four, at sea
he left by the 7.40, was not on the last train back, and came by the 8.05
there is no other train
by her own log she lay at Cardiff from the first to the sixth, loading coal
low water that day was at 10.50 in the morning, and high water not until 5.05
the bar carries water only within two hours of high water
the entry names the New Quay berth
there was no New Quay berth before the first of October

all three are in one hand

the cart went out by the town gate, up Mill Lane
the berths lie inside the quay gate: a cart for a vessel does not pass it
Mr. Garrick writes of casks going to his cellar in Mill Lane
Mr. Pell says he left it on its peg in the lobby
his housekeeper says he came home without it
the fire was meant for the books of the ledger press
the bond ledger was not in the press: it was at Cliff House
Mr. Pell took it after Mr. Prout had gone, and told nobody
the watch made no round at one
whoever sent the boy knew that the pier-head lamp wanted oil
Mr. Odell told that to Mr. Prout and to nobody else
the bell rang at a quarter to two
he was not at the Anchor when it rang
he left at a quarter past one by the taproom clock
the taproom clock is right
the bell was rung at 1.45 by the office clock, which is right too
the cloak hung in the Custom House, for anyone inside to take

Crouch was on the mole
Mr. Pell could not have been on the quay
Mr. Prout had been gone from the Anchor half an hour
the baker knew the man by the cloak, and did not see his face
what the baker saw stands; that it was the Collector was his own conclusion, and it was wrong
Mr. Pell was at Cliff House, the doctor sitting with him
Crouch was on the mole until the bell began
there are two keys to the street door, and the watch has neither
the cloak was found under a boat on the hard, reeking of lamp oil, its hem singed

the first entry was written a month after its date
against: a clerk's honest slips of date

observations.says: the casks went to Mr. Garrick's cellar
at Cardiff, by her log, when the first entry has her at the New Quay
low water an hour before the noon the second entry has her sail at
a berth named a month before it was opened
on all three nights the casks went out by the town gate, and not to a berth
against: a clerk's honest slips of date

observations.says: what the ledger says of the Marigold is not so
the initials on the passes are the clerk's
the casks went to Mr. Garrick's cellar
read as Mr. Prout's, the passes are the clerk letting the casks out under initials that would be taken for the Collector's
the casks went out through the quay gate on those passes
read as Mr. Pell's, the passes are the Collector letting the casks out himself
the fire was set
it was meant for the books of the ledger press
against: out of spite against the Collector

observations.says: the ledger held three false entries
the Surveyor was to compare every export entry with the vessels' papers, two days later
nothing was taken from the iron chest
against: to hide a theft of the duty money

observations.says: only the press was heaped and fired
it was burned to destroy the bond ledger
the false entries were Mr. Prout's to hide
Mr. Prout cleared the quay of its watch
he was seen leaving in the Collector's cloak
the fire-setter did not know the ledger was gone, and Mr. Pell had it himself
the fire-setter knew the house and its lamp room
Captain Venn was at sea

there are two keys to the street door
Mr. Prout says his key has never been out of his pocket
